blocks.text: 1. Model Registry
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506075-365496028.png

Experiment Tracking, the previous topic, identifies the single best candidate model out of many training runs. A Model Registry is where that winning model actually gets managed as it moves toward, and eventually through, production deployment.

It answers a genuinely different question than Experiment Tracking does: not which run was best, but which model is currently deployed, and what came before it. This makes the Model Registry the central, authoritative record of a model's entire lifecycle, from its first promotion out of experimentation all the way through its eventual replacement.
2. Defined Stages
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506075-445171801.png

A model living inside a registry moves through a set of clearly defined stages. Staging holds a candidate model that is currently undergoing final validation, not yet trusted with real production traffic. Production holds the currently deployed model, the one actually, actively serving real predictions right now.

Archived holds a previous production model, retained specifically for rollback and historical reference, rather than being deleted the moment it gets replaced. These clearly named stages give everyone on a team a shared, unambiguous vocabulary for exactly where any given model version currently stands.

blocks.text: 3. What Gets Stored Alongside Each Model

blocks.alt: What Gets Stored Alongside Each Model
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506076-822242378.png

A Model Registry stores the serialized model file itself, using exactly the Serialization and Joblib mechanisms already covered in the Model Deployment module, alongside a direct link back to the exact Experiment Tracking run that originally produced it.

It also stores approval and evaluation records, who reviewed this particular model version, and against what specific criteria, a genuinely important piece of context that turns a bare model file into a fully documented, traceable artifact rather than an anonymous blob of serialized weights.

blocks.text: 4. Versioning Made Concrete

This connects directly back to the version-tracking concern raised throughout the Serialization and Retraining Strategies topics. Every model registered gets a distinct, permanent version number, model v1, v2, v3, and so on, each one still retrievable at any time, never overwritten by whatever version comes after it.

This is precisely what makes Retraining Strategies' rollback plan actually executable in practice, rather than a nice idea with no concrete mechanism behind it. Rolling back means simply pointing the serving system at a previous, already-registered version, a fast, low-risk operation the registry makes directly possible.
5. The Promotion Flow
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506076-123415677.png

A new model completes the Experiment Tracking comparison process and wins as the best available candidate. It gets registered in the Model Registry, entering the Staging stage first, rather than jumping directly into Production without any intermediate checkpoint.

It then undergoes the exact validation already covered in the Retraining Strategies topic, comparing its performance directly against the currently deployed model. If it passes, beating the current champion on the agreed metrics, it gets promoted to Production, and the previous Production model automatically moves to Archived. If it does not pass, it stays in Staging for further work, or gets rejected outright.
6. Why Formal Governance Matters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506077-916845578.png

Formal governance around promotion prevents an unreviewed, unvalidated model from reaching production accidentally, turning what might otherwise be an informal habit, someone just copying a new file into place, into a deliberate, enforced approval step that cannot be skipped by accident.

It also creates a genuine audit trail, useful for both compliance and future debugging: who approved this specific model version, and based on exactly what evidence? This kind of traceable history becomes genuinely valuable the moment anyone needs to understand, months later, exactly how and why a particular model ended up in production.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: Skipping formal registry governance in the name of moving faster often just relocates the risk rather than removing it, an unreviewed model reaching production quietly is exactly the kind of incident a registry's approval step is built to prevent.

blocks.text: 7. How Serving Systems Use the Registry

blocks.alt: How Serving Systems Use the Registry
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506077-18555396.png

This connects back to Real-Time Prediction and Batch Prediction, both covered in the Model Deployment module, and both needing to know exactly which model to actually load at any given moment. A serving system queries the registry for whichever model is currently marked Production, rather than reading from some hardcoded, manually maintained file path.

This decouples the question of which model to serve from any specific file path baked directly into the serving code itself, meaning a new model can be promoted to Production, and immediately picked up by every serving system, without requiring a code change or a new deployment of the serving infrastructure at all.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This decoupling is precisely what lets a Production promotion or a rollback take effect immediately, without needing to redeploy the serving application's own code.

blocks.text: 8. When a Formal Registry Genuinely Earns Its Complexity

blocks.alt: When a Formal Registry Genuinely Earns Its Complexity
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785444506078-815110355.png

A formal Model Registry genuinely earns its complexity for any model that gets retrained and redeployed more than once, since manual, ad hoc file-path tracking simply does not scale reliably beyond a single, first deployment, echoing the exact same scaling concern already raised for ML Pipelines.

It matters just as much under any genuine regulatory or compliance requirement around model changes, where the registry's audit trail becomes a genuinely necessary capability rather than an optional nicety, satisfying a real, external requirement rather than merely an internal preference.

blocks.text: 10. Key Takeaways

items: A Model Registry manages a model as it moves toward and through production, tracking what is currently deployed.
Models move through defined stages: Staging for validation, Production for active serving, Archived for retained history.
A registry stores the model file, a link to its originating experiment run, and approval and evaluation records.
Permanent version numbers make the rollback plan from Retraining Strategies actually executable in practice.
A winning candidate enters Staging, undergoes validation, and only reaches Production if it genuinely beats the current model.
Formal governance prevents accidental unreviewed deployment and creates a genuine, useful audit trail.
Serving systems query the registry for the current Production model, decoupling serving from any hardcoded file path.
A formal registry earns its complexity for repeatedly retrained models and under real compliance requirements.
